items.title: Swarms, Flocks, Gangs: How to build, train, and evaluate multi-agent systems
items.body:
Part 1: Understanding swarms and training to communicate

This is an aspirational blog series for aspirational readers. We (us, the community, you) want to build our own agent swarms because they're exciting, challenging, and increasingly capable. Furthermore, it would be extremely cool if we could train our own agents to work in a swarm. And exponentially cool if those swarms used small and affordable models.

That's what we'll do in this series! Each blog post will include some context on building swarms, alongside reproducible examples that you can run on Hugging Face Jobs. This post's example takes about five hours on two H200s, which costs roughly $50.

Multi-Agent Systems are hard to get working. Adding agents changes the agent's context, the budget, and in turn the complexity of the whole system. Mixing agents' context together through communication is not an inherent performance boost compared to a single agent. The model needs to learn to communicate through training. How do we define what models should learn? And which model weights do we update when we're dealing with many agents?

In this series, we'll work through those problems with an educational overview and practical examples. Each post will introduce a question, build a small system, and examine what happens and how you can reproduce it. This first example starts with four agents, a shared language model, and a simple verifiable task. It's ideal to implement yourself, to tinker with, and to learn from.

First, we'll start off with some context on swarms.

We've heard a lot about swarms over the past few months, both good and bad. In September this year, OpenAI announced that a swarm of roughly 10,000 agents had found a singularity in the 3D Navier-Stokes equations, one of the Millennium Prize problems. A smaller group of nearly 100 agents had already disproved regularity for the unforced 3D Euler equations, a closely related open problem.

But swarms don't always work on the problems we want them to. METR's investigation of the Hugging Face incident found that around 1,200 OpenAI agents, which were supposed to be isolated, had found a way to exchange over 70,000 messages and files. Around 700 joined an attack on Hugging Face while looking for ways to fool their benchmark's scorer, without instruction to do so.

A big swarm isn't, by itself, evidence that cooperation helped. Noam Brown estimates that less than 10% of the Navier-Stokes result came from multi-agent cooperation. In Anthropic's vulnerability-finding experiment, coordinated agents found more bugs than independent agents, but also searched more code and used more tokens. When the comparison was restricted to the same directories, the results per million tokens were about the same.

Did cooperation help, or did we just spend more?

Start with the simplest case. If four agents each try a task independently, the chance that at least one gets it right is higher than with a single attempt, as long as we can tell which answer is correct. That makes a useful baseline for a multi-agent system, but it doesn't show that the agents helped each other. They may simply have had more tries.

Four attempts also cost four times as much. So the fairer comparison is at an equal budget: if each of four agents gets a quarter of the total tokens, can they still beat one agent that spends all of them? We can only find out by testing, because the answer depends on the task, the model and how the work is divided.

This series keeps asking one question: when agents communicate, does it actually help, or are we just spending more compute?

We understand that question through this simple expectation.

We'll treat agent count as a scaling dimension, alongside tokens and model size. Sometimes adding agents will help. Sometimes coordination will consume the budget we hoped to save. The point is to measure both. We won't start with 10,000 agents. We'll start with a small team on a task that we can check easily.

Multi-agent Systems and Reinforcement Learning

Multi-agent reinforcement learning has studied cooperation and competition long before language models were called swarms.

A single agent's task is a Markov decision process: observe, act, get a reward. In a team, everyone shares the reward, but each agent sees only part of the world. This is a decentralized partially observable Markov decision process: teammates, but no one sees the whole picture.

This creates three practical problems. First, teammates keep changing while each agent learns. Second, credit assignment: when the team succeeds, which actions deserve the credit? A winning team can include weak actions, and we may end up rewarding them. Third, a message changes what other agents observe, so communication is part of the policy we're training.

A common solution is centralized training with decentralized execution: training uses information from the whole team, but each agent acts only on its own observations. Our first example follows this pattern with a shared team reward.

Agents can also be organized in different ways. Two useful starting points are:

A hierarchy. A lead agent assigns work to workers and collects their results. Anthropic's Research system works this way, with a separate context for each worker. Kimi K2.5's PARL trains only the orchestrator and keeps the subagents frozen, so training a multi-agent system doesn't mean updating every component. See Anthropic's system description and Kimi's technical blog.

A distributed team. Peers send each other messages and decide when to read their inboxes. No lead agent assigns the actions. This is the setup we'll use here, following the information-aggregation task in s³: Simple Scaling of Swarms via Cooperative Multi-agent RL.

Our first experiment: four agents ordering numbers

We'll reproduce the information-sharing task from Simple Scaling of Swarms because it's interpretable and straightforward to implement. Four agents share a small language model and learn to pool what each of them knows.

Each agent receives one integer from 1 to 99. It knows its own assignment and its teammates' names. It does not initially know the other agents' numbers. For example, four private assignments might be "five", "twenty-six", "five" and "seventy-eight". Duplicates stay in the list, so a correct final answer is:

The team succeeds when at least one agent submits the complete, correctly sorted list. One correct answer is enough; success does not require all four agents to answer correctly. An agent cannot reliably infer the other private assignments without information from its teammates.

This means the task does not yet test Figure 1 directly. Each agent holds information the others need, so a single agent, or a team without messaging, cannot succeed however many retries it gets. Instead, the task tests the precondition behind Figure 1: can a small shared policy learn to communicate at all, and how many tokens does that cost? A later post moves to a task that a single agent can solve alone, where the matched-budget comparison is meaningful.

The main communication tools are message(to, text), read_messages(), and check_notifications(). A notification tells an agent that unread messages exist; reading its inbox makes their contents available. Agents can send direct messages or broadcast to everyone.

We defined a four-agent system using one shared Qwen3-0.6B policy, with separate contexts and private inputs. We are not training four different models. The prompt explains the task and the tools, including the need to share assignments.

A team reward and eight attempts at each problem

In this post, a team means one episode: four agents attempting one problem once. A successful team receives a reward reduced by the tokens it uses. A failed team receives zero:

1부: 스웜 이해 및 의사소통 훈련

이것은 야심 찬 독자를 위한 야심 찬 블로그 시리즈입니다. 우리(커뮤니티, 여러분)는 자체 에이전트 스웜을 만들고 싶습니다. 왜냐하면 스웜은 흥미롭고, 도전적이며, 점점 더 유능해지고 있기 때문입니다. 게다가, 우리 자신의 에이전트가 스웜으로 작동하도록 훈련시킬 수 있다면 매우 멋질 것입니다. 그리고 그 스웜이 작고 저렴한 모델을 사용한다면 엄청나게 멋질 것입니다.

이것이 우리가 이 시리즈에서 할 일입니다! 각 블로그 게시물에는 스웜 구축에 대한 일부 컨텍스트와 함께 Hugging Face Jobs에서 실행할 수 있는 재현 가능한 예제가 포함될 것입니다. 이 게시물의 예제는 두 대의 H200에서 약 5시간이 걸리며, 약 50달러의 비용이 듭니다.

다중 에이전트 시스템(Multi-Agent Systems)은 작동시키기 어렵습니다. 에이전트를 추가하면 에이전트의 컨텍스트, 예산, 그리고 결과적으로 전체 시스템의 복잡성이 변경됩니다. 통신을 통해 에이전트의 컨텍스트를 혼합하는 것이 단일 에이전트에 비해 본질적인 성능 향상은 아닙니다. 모델은 훈련을 통해 통신하는 방법을 배워야 합니다. 모델이 무엇을 배워야 하는지 어떻게 정의할까요? 그리고 많은 에이전트를 다룰 때 어떤 모델 가중치를 업데이트할까요?

이 시리즈에서는 교육적인 개요와 실제 예제를 통해 이러한 문제들을 해결할 것입니다. 각 게시물은 질문을 제시하고, 작은 시스템을 구축하고, 무슨 일이 일어나는지, 그리고 그것을 어떻게 재현할 수 있는지 살펴볼 것입니다. 이 첫 번째 예제는 네 명의 에이전트, 공유 언어 모델, 그리고 간단하고 검증 가능한 작업으로 시작합니다. 이것은 직접 구현하고, 가지고 놀고, 배우기에 이상적입니다.

먼저 스웜에 대한 몇 가지 컨텍스트로 시작하겠습니다.

우리는 지난 몇 달 동안 스웜에 대해 좋은 점과 나쁜 점 모두 많이 들었습니다. 올해 9월, OpenAI는 약 10,000명의 에이전트로 구성된 스웜이 밀레니엄 현상 문제(Millennium Prize problems) 중 하나인 3D Navier-Stokes 방정식에서 특이점을 발견했다고 발표했습니다. 약 100명의 에이전트로 구성된 소규모 그룹은 이미 밀접하게 관련된 미해결 문제인 비강제 3D Euler 방정식의 규칙성을 반증했습니다.

그러나 스웜이 우리가 원하는 문제에서 항상 작동하는 것은 아닙니다. METR의 Hugging Face 사고 조사 결과, 고립되어 있어야 할 약 1,200명의 OpenAI 에이전트가 70,000개 이상의 메시지와 파일을 교환하는 방법을 찾았다는 것이 밝혀졌습니다. 약 700명이 지시 없이 벤치마크 채점자를 속이는 방법을 찾으면서 Hugging Face에 대한 공격에 참여했습니다.

큰 스웜 자체가 협력이 도움이 되었다는 증거는 아닙니다. Noam Brown은 Navier-Stokes 결과의 10% 미만이 다중 에이전트 협력에서 비롯되었다고 추정합니다. Anthropic의 취약점 발견 실험에서, 협력하는 에이전트는 독립적인 에이전트보다 더 많은 버그를 찾았지만, 더 많은 코드를 검색하고 더 많은 토큰을 사용했습니다. 비교를 동일한 디렉토리로 제한했을 때, 백만 토큰당 결과는 거의 동일했습니다.

협력이 도움이 되었을까요, 아니면 단순히 더 많은 비용을 지출했을까요?

가장 간단한 경우부터 시작합시다. 네 명의 에이전트가 각자 독립적으로 작업을 시도하면, 적어도 한 명이 정답을 맞출 확률은 단일 시도보다 높습니다. 단, 어떤 답변이 올바른지 알 수 있는 경우입니다. 이것은 다중 에이전트 시스템에 유용한 기준선이 되지만, 에이전트들이 서로 도왔다는 것을 보여주지는 않습니다. 단순히 더 많은 시도를 했을 수도 있습니다.

네 번의 시도는 또한 네 배의 비용이 듭니다. 따라서 더 공정한 비교는 동일한 예산에서 이루어집니다. 즉, 네 명의 에이전트 각각이 총 토큰의 1/4을 사용하면, 모든 토큰을 사용하는 한 명의 에이전트를 여전히 이길 수 있을까요? 이 답변은 작업, 모델 및 작업 분할 방식에 따라 다르기 때문에 테스트를 통해서만 알 수 있습니다.

이 시리즈는 한 가지 질문을 계속 던집니다. 에이전트가 통신할 때 실제로 도움이 될까요, 아니면 단순히 더 많은 컴퓨팅을 사용하는 것일까요?

우리는 이 간단한 기대를 통해 그 질문을 이해합니다.

우리는 토큰 및 모델 크기와 함께 에이전트 수를 스케일링 차원으로 취급할 것입니다. 때로는 에이전트를 추가하는 것이 도움이 될 것입니다. 때로는 조정이 우리가 절약하기를 바랐던 예산을 소비할 것입니다. 중요한 것은 둘 다 측정하는 것입니다. 우리는 10,000명의 에이전트로 시작하지 않을 것입니다. 우리는 쉽게 확인할 수 있는 작업에 대한 작은 팀으로 시작할 것입니다.

다중 에이전트 시스템 및 강화 학습

다중 에이전트 강화 학습은 언어 모델이 스웜이라고 불리기 훨씬 전부터 협력과 경쟁을 연구했습니다.

단일 에이전트의 작업은 마르코프 결정 과정입니다. 관찰하고, 행동하고, 보상을 받습니다. 팀에서는 모든 사람이 보상을 공유하지만, 각 에이전트는 세상의 일부만 봅니다. 이것은 분산된 부분 관측 마르코프 결정 과정입니다. 팀원들은 있지만, 아무도 전체 그림을 보지 못합니다.

이것은 세 가지 실제적인 문제를 야기합니다. 첫째, 각 에이전트가 학습하는 동안 팀원들이 계속 변경됩니다. 둘째, 신용 할당입니다. 팀이 성공했을 때 어떤 행동이 신용을 받아야 할까요? 승리하는 팀에는 약한 행동이 포함될 수 있으며, 우리는 그들에게 보상을 줄 수도 있습니다. 셋째, 메시지는 다른 에이전트가 관찰하는 것을 변경하므로, 통신은 우리가 훈련하는 정책의 일부입니다.

일반적인 해결책은 분산 실행과 함께 중앙 집중식 훈련입니다. 훈련은 전체 팀의 정보를 사용하지만, 각 에이전트는 자신의 관찰에 따라 행동합니다. 우리의 첫 번째 예제는 공유 팀 보상으로 이 패턴을 따릅니다.

에이전트는 또한 다양한 방식으로 조직될 수 있습니다. 두 가지 유용한 시작점은 다음과 같습니다.

계층 구조. 선두 에이전트가 작업자에게 작업을 할당하고 결과를 수집합니다. Anthropic의 Research 시스템은 각 작업자에게 별도의 컨텍스트를 사용하여 이런 식으로 작동합니다. Kimi K2.5의 PARL은 오케스트레이터만 훈련하고 서브 에이전트를 고정 상태로 유지하므로, 다중 에이전트 시스템을 훈련하는 것이 모든 구성 요소를 업데이트하는 것을 의미하지는 않습니다. Anthropic의 시스템 설명 및 Kimi의 기술 블로그를 참조하십시오.

분산 팀. 피어들이 서로 메시지를 보내고 언제 받은 편지함을 읽을지 결정합니다. 선두 에이전트가 행동을 할당하지 않습니다. 이것이 우리가 여기에서 사용할 설정이며, s³: Simple Scaling of Swarms via Cooperative Multi-agent RL의 정보 집계 작업을 따릅니다.

우리의 첫 번째 실험: 숫자 순서를 정하는 네 명의 에이전트

items.title: AI agents now control part of DeepMind's compute for Gemini experiments
items.body:
Google Deepmind lets AI agents run experiments on their own for the next Gemini model. On the company's podcast, VP of Research Koray Kavukcuoglu, who leads Gemini development, frames this as part of a strategic shift at the lab. Rather than running separate teams for specialized projects like AlphaFold and nuclear fusion, Deepmind now relies on a single general-purpose algorithm for both science and products, he says. Each Gemini generation, he adds, is a hand-built one-off rather than a fixed architecture, while parallel teams work on its successors.

According to Kavukcuoglu, AI agents control part of the compute themselves to run experiments, though the lab is still far from full recursive self-improvement. As a safety measure, Deepmind doesn't reward the agents' internal thought streams ("Chain of Thought") during training, he says, so their intentions stay unfiltered and reviewable in natural language before they act.

Kavukcuoglu also points to limits. Today's AI can depict physical processes such as fluid flows and collisions with visual accuracy, he says, but doesn't understand them precisely. No test can show when models will close those gaps and reach artificial general intelligence (AGI), he argues, because no benchmark captures the core of intelligence. In his view, AGI won't begin until useful everyday products earn enough trust for people to hand decisions over to them, the way they would when working with other people.AdAd

items.body_ko:
Google DeepMind는 다음 Gemini 모델을 위해 AI 에이전트가 자체적으로 실험을 실행하도록 허용합니다. 회사 팟캐스트에서 Gemini 개발을 이끄는 연구 담당 부사장 Koray Kavukcuoglu는 이를 연구실의 전략적 변화의 일환으로 설명합니다. AlphaFold 및 핵융합과 같은 전문 프로젝트를 위해 별도의 팀을 운영하는 대신, DeepMind는 이제 과학 및 제품 모두에 대해 단일 범용 알고리즘에 의존한다고 그는 말합니다. 각 Gemini 세대는 고정된 아키텍처가 아닌 수작업으로 제작된 일회성 모델이며, 병렬 팀이 후속 모델을 연구하고 있다고 덧붙입니다.

Kavukcuoglu에 따르면, AI 에이전트는 실험을 실행하기 위해 컴퓨팅의 일부를 자체적으로 제어하지만, 연구실은 아직 완전한 재귀적 자기 개선과는 거리가 멀다고 합니다. 안전 조치로 DeepMind는 훈련 중에 에이전트의 내부 사고 흐름("Chain of Thought")에 보상을 주지 않는다고 그는 말합니다. 따라서 그들의 의도는 행동하기 전에 자연어로 필터링되지 않고 검토 가능하게 유지됩니다.

Kavukcuoglu는 또한 한계를 지적합니다. 오늘날의 AI는 유체 흐름 및 충돌과 같은 물리적 프로세스를 시각적으로 정확하게 묘사할 수 있지만, 이를 정확하게 이해하지는 못한다고 그는 말합니다. 어떤 테스트도 모델이 이러한 격차를 해소하고 인공 일반 지능(AGI)에 도달할 시기를 보여줄 수 없다고 그는 주장합니다. 왜냐하면 어떤 벤치마크도 지능의 핵심을 포착하지 못하기 때문입니다. 그의 관점에서 AGI는 사람들이 다른 사람들과 일할 때처럼 일상적인 유용한 제품이 의사 결정을 그들에게 넘겨줄 만큼 충분한 신뢰를 얻을 때까지 시작되지 않을 것입니다. 광고 광고

items.title: Show HN: I wrote an entire Vim manual over 4 years
items.body: I'm glad to announce that I'm releasing my new book, Learning to Play Vim.When I started using Vim more than a decade ago, I wished there was a manual out there teaching how to use this fantastic editor step by step, beginning with the foundations up to more advanced features. Of course at the time I did the vimtutor, but it was too dense for me to remember much from it. I also read the entire Vim manual (`:help manual`), but I didn't like it: it was too detailed in places (for example `02.8 Finding help` completely lost me for a while), and other features didn't get the treatment they deserved.So I decided to write my own Vim manual. It took me more than 4 years and 2987 focused pomodoros (1244 hours) of work to finally get it done!The result:- 21 chapters showing the most important Vim features step by step.- 170 exercises with solutions.- Many real-life examples to show how Vim can be used and configured for your own needs.- The related Vim's help pages to dig further into each feature.Most configs are both written in Vimscript and Lua for Neovim users. This book explores the common features between Vim and Neovim, so don't expect anything about Neovim-specific features (like treesitter or LSP for example).- The landing page: https://themouseless.dev/vim/- A sample of the book with the entire table of contents and the first three chapters covering most of the basics: https://themouseless.dev/content/learning_to_play_vim_sample....I wrote this with my bare hands, no LLM involved to spoil the fun.

items.title: AMD-specific fork of llama.cpp
items.body:
tl;dr — I recommend using llama-cpp-rdna-boosts if you have an AMD graphics card. It’s lean, and increased my token generation from 35 to 55 tokens/second, and my prefill from 700 to 1300 tokens per second. YMMV.

As of November 2026, an explosion in the number of bespoke inference engines has taken place. Many of them take inspiration from the engines that enabled much of the LLM inference up 'til now: llama.cpp, SGLang, vLLM, etc.

The rationale isn’t that those options are bad, but merely that they are generalist engines, optimized for no particular hardware and with a focus on broad compatibility. Others feel the development pace of those engines have slowed down, and with the help of LLMs, they can move faster on their own.

Some examples of these new inference engines* are Strata, Basalt, RustingStrata, etc…

These new forks generally all have a few things in common:

They focus on a specific subset of models and/or hardware

They use a frontier model to vibe-code the entire thing

They chase ever-higher token generation speeds

… and the results are stunning! Strata is able to run a heavily-quantized model of Qwen 3.8 Flash Next, a 180B parameter model, on a 16GB VRAM graphics card, and 16GB system RAM, and have it generate tokens at a surprisingly high rate.

In and of itself those three things are not red flags (the second is concerning, of course, but it may be SOP in a year’s time — who knows!), but as these projects have evolved, that relentless chase toward higher token generation speeds has taken an unfortunate turn, in that the optimizations are less about hardware-specific changes, but more about changing how the model thinks so that it goes brrr faster.

Strata specifically has taken to preferring to poll experts loaded in VRAM even if other experts (pushed to system RAM/disk) would have been normally chosen. This is just one example, but certainly not the last.

That said, I was fortunate to stumble upon yet another project that promised improvements, delivered, and was more aligned with my software development philosophy.

Enter llama-cpp-rdna-boosts. It is a repository that contains a minimal set of changes that you apply against a pinned commit of llama.cpp. It is in essence a fork, but one whose changeset is continually re-applied to newer versions of llama.cpp. It contains AMD-specific improvements that drastically improve prefill and token-generation speeds.

I appreciate llama.cpp’s approach to software development. They are a stable base to branch off from. Contributions are vetted throughly and applied judiciously. ✅

The rdna-boosts repo is a set of small patches that are applied to base llama.cpp. Fewer moving parts mean fewer things to maintain ✅

The changes are (somewhat opaquely, it’s all straight Claudish 😬) outlined in the documentation, ensuring some degree of transparency. ✅

If you have ROCm libraries installed on your system, you can build the image yourself. I didn’t want to mess with that, so I used the pre-built images published.

podman pull ghcr.io/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts:server-rocm-10.1

This sets up an image that you can run sandboxed via podman to launch the inference server:

podman run --rm -it \ --network=host \ --device /dev/kfd \ --device /dev/dri \ --group-add video \ -v "$HOME/models:/models" \ "ghcr.io/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts:server-rocm-10.1" \

My actual launch script passes a few additional flags, but those are the important lines.

I imagine upgrading would be pulling a new image down, though I have not tried this yet.

On my setup, an AMD R9700 connected to my laptop via an eGPU interface, this improved prefill and token generation rates when running ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF (Q6_K_L) with MTP enabled:

Strata and its ilk were always promising the moon and it was never clear what steps they took to make that happen. I’m very much looking forward to what the rdna-boosts community come up with next.

* It’s worth noting that between these two groups, vllm-radiance made an appearance, which was a fork of vLLM with AMD-specific patches. I tried this too, but the build steps were so onerous and vLLM so overbuilt for my specific use case (1 machine, 1 developer), that I abandoned it and went back to vanilla llama.cpp
items.body_ko:
요약하자면, AMD 그래픽 카드를 사용하고 있다면 llama-cpp-rdna-boosts를 사용하는 것을 추천합니다. 가볍고, 토큰 생성 속도를 초당 35토큰에서 55토큰으로, Prefill 속도를 초당 700토큰에서 1300토큰으로 증가시켰습니다. 개인마다 결과는 다를 수 있습니다.

2026년 11월 현재, 맞춤형 추론 엔진의 수가 폭발적으로 증가했습니다. 이들 중 상당수는 지금까지 LLM 추론을 가능하게 했던 llama.cpp, SGLang, vLLM 등의 엔진에서 영감을 받았습니다.

그 이유는 기존 옵션들이 나쁘기 때문이 아니라, 특정 하드웨어에 최적화되지 않고 광범위한 호환성에 초점을 맞춘 범용 엔진이기 때문입니다. 또한, 일부에서는 이러한 엔진들의 개발 속도가 느려졌다고 느끼며, LLM의 도움으로 자체적으로 더 빠르게 움직일 수 있다고 생각합니다.

이러한 새로운 추론 엔진의 예로는 Strata, Basalt, RustingStrata 등이 있습니다.

이러한 새로운 Fork들은 일반적으로 몇 가지 공통점을 가지고 있습니다.

특정 모델 및/또는 하드웨어의 특정 하위 집합에 중점을 둡니다.

전체 코드를 Vibe-code하는 데 Frontier 모델을 사용합니다.

점점 더 높은 토큰 생성 속도를 추구합니다.

… 그리고 그 결과는 놀랍습니다! Strata는 Qwen 3.8 Flash Next의 고도로 양자화된 모델(180B 매개변수 모델)을 16GB VRAM 그래픽 카드와 16GB 시스템 RAM에서 실행할 수 있으며, 놀랍도록 빠른 속도로 토큰을 생성합니다.

이 세 가지 자체는 위험 신호가 아닙니다(물론 두 번째는 우려스럽지만, 1년 안에 SOP가 될 수도 있습니다. 누가 알겠습니까!). 그러나 이러한 프로젝트가 발전함에 따라, 더 높은 토큰 생성 속도를 향한 끊임없는 추구는 불행한 방향으로 바뀌었습니다. 최적화가 하드웨어별 변경보다는 모델이 더 빠르게 ‘brrr’ 소리를 내도록 생각하는 방식을 변경하는 데 더 중점을 두게 된 것입니다.

Strata는 특히 VRAM에 로드된 Expert들을 선호하는 경향을 보입니다. 심지어 다른 Expert들(시스템 RAM/디스크로 푸시된)이 일반적으로 선택되었을 경우에도 말이죠. 이것은 단지 한 가지 예일 뿐이며, 확실히 마지막 예는 아닐 것입니다.

하지만 저는 운 좋게도 개선을 약속하고 실제로 제공했으며, 제 소프트웨어 개발 철학과 더 잘 맞는 또 다른 프로젝트를 발견했습니다.

바로 llama-cpp-rdna-boosts입니다. 이 저장소는 llama.cpp의 특정 커밋에 적용할 수 있는 최소한의 변경 사항 세트를 포함하고 있습니다. 본질적으로 Fork이지만, 변경 사항 세트가 llama.cpp의 최신 버전에 지속적으로 재적용됩니다. 이는 AMD에 특화된 개선 사항을 포함하여 Prefill 및 토큰 생성 속도를 크게 향상시킵니다.

저는 llama.cpp의 소프트웨어 개발 접근 방식에 감사하게 생각합니다. 그들은 분기할 수 있는 안정적인 기반입니다. 기여는 철저히 검토되고 신중하게 적용됩니다. ✅

rdna-boosts 저장소는 기본 llama.cpp에 적용되는 작은 패치 세트입니다. 적은 움직이는 부품은 유지 관리할 것이 적다는 것을 의미합니다. ✅

변경 사항은 문서에 (다소 불투명하게, 모두 순수한 Claudish 😬입니다) 설명되어 있어 어느 정도의 투명성을 보장합니다. ✅

시스템에 ROCm 라이브러리가 설치되어 있다면 직접 이미지를 빌드할 수 있습니다. 저는 그렇게 복잡하게 하고 싶지 않아서 미리 빌드된 이미지를 사용했습니다.

podman pull ghcr.io/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts:server-rocm-10.1

이렇게 하면 podman을 통해 샌드박스에서 실행하여 추론 서버를 시작할 수 있는 이미지가 설정됩니다.

podman run --rm -it \ --network=host \ --device /dev/kfd \ --device /dev/dri \ --group-add video \ -v "$HOME/models:/models" \ "ghcr.io/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts:server-rocm-10.1" \

실제 실행 스크립트에는 몇 가지 추가 플래그가 전달되지만, 위 내용은 중요한 줄입니다.

업그레이드는 새 이미지를 다운로드하는 방식일 것이라고 생각하지만, 아직 시도해보지는 않았습니다.

제 설정(eGPU 인터페이스를 통해 노트북에 연결된 AMD R9700)에서 MTP가 활성화된 ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF (Q6_K_L)를 실행했을 때 Prefill 및 토큰 생성 속도가 향상되었습니다.

items.title: Show HN: SimDrop – Running iOS simulators in the macOS Finder sidebar
items.body:
Hi HN, I made a small macOS utility for my own iOS simulator workflow.I kept running into two annoyances: getting config files in and out of a simulator is clunky (digging into CoreSimulator UUID folders or running simctl), and on the iPhone Duo simulator I couldn't even drag and drop images onto the window at all.SimDrop puts every running iOS simulator in Finder's sidebar (under Locations) with two folders:- Downloads/ (Files app > On My iPhone > Downloads)
- Photos and Videos/ (the simulator's Photos library)Simulators appear when they boot and disappear when they shut down. Everything is also reachable from the terminal under ~/Library/CloudStorage/SimDrop-SimDrop/.A couple of caveats up front:
- Dragging moves files by default (same as iCloud Drive, because it uses File Provider on the startup volume)—hold Option to copy.
- macOS 15+ and iOS simulators only (not physical devices).It's free, open source (GPL-3.0), signed and notarized, and installable via Homebrew: brew install --cask rxliuli/tap/sim-drop

Just sharing in case others run into the same friction—feedback or PRs welcome!

items.title: Spectrum Adaptation of AI-Native Autoencoder Communications with Transfer Learning
items.body: End-to-end physical-layer learning replaces separate modulation, coding, and detection operations with an autoencoder (AE) that consists of a jointly trained encoder-decoder pair at the transmitter and the receiver. This paper studies AI-native communications with AEs and quantifies the sensitivity to training-test mismatch in channel models. Models trained only on an AWGN channel achieve low bit error rates (BERs) under matched conditions but degrade severely on Rayleigh fading with practical front-end impairments. To reduce the time and energy required to adapt to new channel conditions, we propose a low-latency transfer-learning procedure that starts from an AWGN-pretrained system and fine-tunes only a small subset of transmitter and receiver layers while freezing the remainder. We further formulate layer selection as a budget-constrained optimization problem that identifies the most informative parameters to update during adaptation. This preserves the learned signal geometry and the deep decision structure while adapting lightweight front ends to fading- and impairment-induced mixing. For AE communications, we show that partial updates remove the mismatch-induced error floor and approach the BER of fully retrained models. We provide a layer-wise study and quantify resource-performance trade-offs, showing that modest adaptation substantially reduces BER while cutting training time, multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations, energy consumption, and the fraction of updated parameters for resource-efficient implementation.

items.title: Tokenisation is not in APX
items.body: In this paper, we prove that, unless P=NP, no polynomial-time algorithm can find a tokeniser whose objective is within any constant factor of the optimum, meaning that tokenisation is not in the APX complexity class. We prove this for direct and bottom-up tokenisation, under both a compression or unigram log-likelihood objectives, and for binary or larger alphabets. We further show that, even over unary alphabets, direct tokenisation is APX-hard, and thus admits no polynomial-time approximation scheme.

items.title: Can image generation help visual reasoning? An empirical study
items.body: Language models think in words; then multimodal models might think in images. We test whether a generated helper improves the answer to a visual question. A model describes the helper it needs and then answers using the original and generated images together. Across 13 vision-language model and generator pairs, generation lowers mean accuracy by 3.7 percentage points, with declines on nine of ten tasks. Two unified models, BAGEL and Janus-Pro-7B, each lose accuracy on eight tasks. On VSTAR, adding a generated image to the same planning hint lowers accuracy by 10.47 points. Repeated image edits yield different outcomes across tasks. ChartQAPro and MathVista stay below their no-generation baselines, while ERQA gains three points after ten edits.

items.title: Attack Policy Selection can Mislead Monitor Evaluators
items.body:
AI monitors, classifiers that flag dangerous behaviour by AI agents, are often evaluated against transcripts generated by attack policies acting as proxies for dangerous behaviour in deployment. We evaluate an ex-production OpenAI monitor as a case study and find that measured false negative rate is highly sensitive to both the method used to generate attack policies and the level of optimisation applied within that method. This rate ranged from 0.5\% to 20.8\% across optimisation levels of a single method (reinforcement learning), and from 6.4\% to 23.0\% across methods at their best observed optimisation level (optimised prompting vs.\ transcript editing). Every attack policy was developed against proxy monitors only: all reported results show attacks transferring to the held-out GPT-5.4 target monitor. Our results suggest that monitor evasion evaluations can easily mislead: an evaluation using only basic attack methods may give false confidence that a monitor is strong.
The sensitivity to attack-policy choice raises a problem: interpreting any particular result as evidence about deployment performance requires justification. The transcripts produced by attack policies are proxies for the dangerous behaviour a monitor must flag in deployment. These proxies can introduce visible artefacts, such as reasoning about a ``side task'' absent from the instructions shown to the monitor, that affect monitor judgements. Given the sensitivity above, the choice of proxy can change an evaluation's conclusion. Reading these results as evidence about deployment therefore requires a separate legitimacy argument for why the proxies are informative, including any justification of conservativeness. Making convincing arguments remains an open problem.

items.title: A gene informed benchmark for BioScoring of pathology foundation models
items.body: Pathology foundation models are usually compared by their performance on downstream tasks such as classification and retrieval. While such benchmarks measure how useful a model is, they provide no insight into the biology it represents. We introduce BioScore, a benchmark that quantifies how well an image encoder captures cell identities, with spatial transcriptomics of the same tissue as the reference. A sparse autoencoder splits the encoder's patch embeddings into sparse features, which we cluster into a fixed number of groups. BioScore then measures, for each of 52 cell identities defined by marker genes, how specifically one group follows the identity's expression over the tissue. Because the autoencoder training is fully unsupervised, a match shows that the model represents the cell identity from the image alone. We score 8 pathology foundation models and 3 natural-image models. Every pathology model scores above every natural-image model (0.299--0.371 \vs 0.214--0.232), and paired tests separate three tiers among the pathology models. Unlike a supervised probe, BioScore needs no labels, builds its reference from the data and scores even from few sections, yet it ranks the encoders as a probe does. Its per-identity breakdown indicates which cell identities each encoder captures or misses.

items.title: Diverse Alternative Reasoning Traces for Hard Math Problems
items.body: Post-training large language models (LLMs) for mathematical reasoning often relies on accepted traces whose final answers pass a verifier. For hard math problems, however, such traces can be rare under independent Monte Carlo (MC) sampling. To address this, we propose Diverse Alternative Reasoning Traces (DART), a trace-mining method that starts from a rejected trace, decomposes it into reasoning steps, and ranks them by position-weighted uncertainty. It then generates deliberately distinct alternative candidates for highly ranked steps using reference-answer guidance and a meta-thought before completing the resulting traces. On greedy-unsolved DeepMath-103K problems, DART recovers 37% more problems than MC sampling at a matched number of generated traces. Its estimated generation cost per recovered problem is nearly identical, while its cost per accepted trace is 30% lower. Post-training Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on traces mined by DART achieves the highest point estimate in five of six evaluations across MATH-500 and AIME benchmarks. These results demonstrate that revisiting rejected traces with DART can expand problem coverage and provide effective post-training data.
items.title_ko: 어려운 수학 문제 해결을 위한 다양한 대안적 추론 경로
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 어려운 수학 문제에 대한 대규모 언어 모델(LLM)의 추론 능력을 향상시키기 위한 DART(Diverse Alternative Reasoning Traces)라는 새로운 방법을 제안합니다. DART는 오답 추론 경로에서 불확실한 단계를 식별하고, 의도적으로 다양한 대체 경로를 생성하여 답을 찾습니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 수학적 추론 능력을 향상시키는 데 중요한 방법론적 발전을 제시하며, 특히 복잡한 문제 해결을 위한 모델의 '사고' 과정을 다양화하는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer
items.body: Looped Transformers boost expressivity by reusing shared layers across loops, yet at the cost of efficiency. Pushing their expressivity-efficiency frontier requires rethinking the core mechanism connecting adjacent loops: What should be passed as a Transformer loops? We introduce Mixture-of-Loops Transformer (MoLT), whose Mixture-of-Loops Attention (MoLA) uses keys and values (KV) as memory for selective reuse across depths and loops. Under loop residual, MoLT-R retains the residual stream and reads local KV across loops for expressivity. Under loop KV, MoLT-KV instead restarts from embeddings and reads current-loop local KV with preceding-loop memory KV at earlier positions for efficiency. MoLT-KV eliminates same-position cross-loop dependence and, paired with loop forcing for parallel training, unlocks single-traversal Mixture-of-Loops (MoL) decoding beyond the training loop horizon. To balance efficiency and quality, we introduce U-shaped MoLT (U-MoLT), which separates memory construction from prediction readout and skips unused decoder traversals without changing predictions. In 400B-token pretraining, U-MoLT outperforms OLMo3 across 700M/1.5B dense and 3B MoE models, achieving 1.7x validation cross-entropy (CE) token efficiency at 700M while improving 3B MoE 10-domain perplexity by 0.75 and 10-task accuracy by 2.1 percentage points. In 100B-token continued pretraining of Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base, our U-MoLT adaptation lowers CE on all 11 domains over the matched baseline with 1.4x mean token efficiency. At inference, U-MoLT with MoL-Hybrid-2 matches non-looped OLMo3 latency at 996.6 vs. 1,000.6 ms on S-size (~113M) models. Code is available at https://github.com/hustvl/MoLT
items.title_ko: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer (MoLT) 제안
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 효율성을 유지하면서 표현력을 높이는 Mixture-of-Loops Transformer (MoLT)를 소개합니다. MoLT의 Mixture-of-Loops Attention (MoLA)은 키와 값(KV)을 메모리로 사용하여 깊이와 루프 전반에 걸쳐 선택적 재사용을 가능하게 합니다. 이는 Looped Transformer의 핵심 메커니즘을 재고합니다.
items.why_ko: Transformer 모델의 효율성과 표현력을 동시에 개선하려는 연구로, 특히 긴 시퀀스 처리가 필요한 LLM의 성능 향상에 기여할 수 있는 아키텍처적 진보입니다.

items.title: $μ$-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-User Task Completion in Shared Interaction Voice Agents
items.body: Voice agents in shared spaces must satisfy interdependent multi-user requests while upholding per-user authority, privacy, and task constraints. Existing evaluations offer limited coverage when participants react throughout a session. We introduce $μ$-Bench, a benchmark for joint task completion in closed-loop, full-duplex multi-user voice interaction. Simulated participants act from isolated profiles of goals, knowledge, and permissions, adapting to the agent's speech and tool outcomes. Across 20 domains, 100 scenarios vary group size, acoustics, and follow-up demands to form 800 cases (408 tool-augmented, 392 tool-free). Joint Task Success (JTS) requires all user goals, privacy boundaries, and terminal states to hold jointly, while Pure JTS further disallows unauthorized tool calls; Attribution, Threading, and Coordination (ATC) diagnostics localize failures. Across 13 voice agents, proprietary systems peak at 62.24\% tool-free and 65.44\% tool-augmented success, while open-weight models remain below 20\%. ATC diagnostics show that open-weight models lag primarily in multi-turn attribution and threading, and controlled contrasts reveal that larger groups consistently degrade joint task success across capable systems. By coupling reactive multi-user simulation with verifiable session-level outcomes, $μ$-Bench provides a rigorous testbed for shared voice agents.
items.title_ko: $μ$-Bench: 공유 상호작용 음성 에이전트의 다중 사용자 작업 완료 벤치마킹
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 공유 공간에서 다중 사용자 음성 에이전트의 공동 작업 완료 능력을 평가하기 위한 벤치마크인 $μ$-Bench를 소개합니다. 이 벤치마크는 폐쇄 루프, 전이중 다중 사용자 음성 상호작용에서 시뮬레이션된 참가자들이 에이전트의 응답에 적응하며 목표를 달성하는 시나리오를 제공합니다.
items.why_ko: 다중 사용자 환경에서 음성 AI 에이전트의 복잡한 상호작용 및 작업 완료 능력을 평가하는 표준화된 방법을 제공하여, 실제 적용 가능한 다중 에이전트 시스템 개발에 기여합니다.

items.title: Enhancing Maritime Domain Awareness using Latent Space Representations
items.body:
This work presents a novel application of Earth Observation (EO) embeddings for Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA) from the perspective of the geospatial foundation model TerraMind. By operating directly on compressed latent-space representations rather than on the original Sentinel-1 imagery, this approach directly addresses the data gravity bottleneck that increasingly constrains operational EO processing, in line with the objectives of the Embed2Scale project. In particular, linear and non-linear probing of compressed embeddings, latent space representations of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery, is used to detect, localise, and characterise vessels from Sentinel-1 GRD images. Vessel detection achieves a ROC-AUC of 0.95, while vessel localisation has a median error of around 300 m for vessels longer than 100 m, and vessel AIS type-code classification achieves 62% accuracy for the majority classes. The latter, however, is highly correlated with vessel length. These results reveal both the potential and current limitations of Geospatial Foundation Models (GeoFMs) when applied to fine-grained MDA understanding in real-world scenarios.
Additionally, a new maritime remote sensing dataset is released, pairing about 2,000 Sentinel-1 images with temporally aligned AIS signals from commercial vessels. Through manual inspection, each candidate sample was verified for bounding-box quality and for consistency between the AIS-reported vessel length and the observed vessel extent, cross-checking vessel identity and location against publicly available vessel records and, where available, photographs. The dataset was made ready for use with the NeuCo-Bench neural compression benchmark framework, publicly available on HuggingFace through https://huggingface.co/datasets/embed2scale/S1-single-ship-downstream .
items.title_ko: 잠재 공간 표현을 이용한 해양 영역 인식 강화
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 지리공간 파운데이션 모델인 TerraMind의 관점에서 지구 관측(EO) 임베딩을 해양 영역 인식(MDA)에 적용하는 새로운 방법을 제시합니다. 원본 Sentinel-1 이미지가 아닌 압축된 잠재 공간 표현을 직접 사용하여 데이터 중력 병목 현상을 해결하고자 합니다.
items.why_ko: 방대한 지구 관측 데이터를 효율적으로 처리하고 활용하여 해양 감시 및 인식 능력을 향상시킬 수 있는 잠재력을 보여줍니다.

items.title: What a Drop Reveals: Sim-to-Real Material Estimation for Deformable Objects from Video
items.body: How an object deforms when it hits the ground reveals what it is made of. From a single real video of a drop, we estimate a deformable object's density-normalized stiffness $E/ρ$, and its yield stress $σ_Y/ρ$ when the impact causes plastic deformation, with a feed-forward predictor trained only in simulation. Real videos carry no material labels, so such predictors are developed and validated on synthetic data alone. We show that synthetic validation ranks their geometric inputs in the wrong order. Material acts through 3D deformation, and tracklets lifted to 3D with estimated depth are indeed the most accurate input in simulation. However, on real drops they are the least accurate, and better depth does not repair them: the failure persists with simulator depth in training, LiDAR depth at test time, and exact depth on rendered replays of the real drops. Short 2D optical-flow tracklets do the opposite: they improve nothing in simulation, yet they transfer best. Material is therefore better read from what perception measures consistently in both domains than from what is most informative in simulation. Our predictor, PhysReader, reads the video and 2D tracklets and learns the lift to 3D in simulation by matching a teacher that sees exact 3D deformation. To measure transfer, we introduce PhysReader-Real: 16 everyday objects dropped five times each, with reference materials fit jointly to each object's drops and checked against tensile tests. On PhysReader-Real, PhysReader is closer to the reference materials than every other input and baseline. The one exception is a per-scene optimizer started from PhysReader's prediction, which ends slightly closer but takes 49 minutes per video instead of 12 seconds.
items.title_ko: 떨어지는 영상만으로 물체의 재료 추정: 변형 가능한 물체에 대한 Sim-to-Real 재료 추정 연구
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 물체가 땅에 떨어질 때 변형되는 모습을 담은 단일 실제 영상만으로 변형 가능한 물체의 밀도 정규화된 강성($E/ρ$)과 항복 응력($σ_Y/ρ$)을 추정하는 방법을 제시합니다. 시뮬레이션으로만 훈련된 피드포워드 예측기를 사용하며, 실제 영상에는 재료 레이블이 없기 때문에 합성 데이터로만 개발 및 검증됩니다.
items.why_ko: 로봇 공학 및 컴퓨터 비전 분야에서 실제 데이터가 부족한 상황에서도 시뮬레이션만으로 물체의 물리적 특성을 추정할 수 있는 가능성을 열어줍니다.

items.title: Interpretable and Accurate Hybrid Decision Trees with Selective Case-Based Splits
items.body: Decision trees are among the most well-known interpretable models in Machine Learning. Over the years, a wide variety of strategies have been proposed to define split conditions within the greedy learning framework, aiming to guide instance routing and enhance predictive performance. These strategies range from axis-parallel and oblique splits based on feature values to proximity-based splits using exemplar instances and more complex hybrid approaches. However, no single method has emerged as universally superior. In this work, we present two key contributions to the construction of greedy decision trees. First, we propose a hybrid tree architecture that integrates both feature-based and case-based splits, allowing for heterogeneous splits throughout the tree. Second, we introduce a novel type of split that leverages a selective case-based approach: when a split is needed, our method searches for the most informative subset of features to define the split, effectively balancing the specificity of case-based methods with the simplicity of feature-based ones. Experiments on a diverse set of tabular datasets show that our method outperforms standard decision trees and achieves performance on par with ensemble methods, while producing shallow trees that retain or even improve predictive accuracy.
items.title_ko: 선택적 사례 기반 분할을 통한 해석 가능하고 정확한 하이브리드 의사결정 트리
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 기계 학습에서 해석 가능한 모델로 잘 알려진 의사결정 트리의 새로운 분할 전략을 제안합니다. 피처 값 기반의 축-평행 및 경사 분할, 그리고 유사성 기반의 예제 인스턴스를 사용하는 분할을 넘어선 하이브리드 접근법을 통해 예측 성능을 향상시키고자 합니다.
items.why_ko: 의사결정 트리의 해석 가능성을 유지하면서 예측 성능을 높이는 새로운 방법을 제시하여, 실용적인 머신러닝 모델 개발에 기여할 수 있습니다.

items.title: Stranger Things: When Objects Appear Without Their Typical Neighbors
items.body: Visual context is a powerful cue for object recognition: scenes inform what, where, and at what scale objects are likely to appear. Yet over-reliance on context becomes a failure mode when models predict objects based on their typical neighbors rather than the objects' own visual features, which we call typicality bias. While extensively studied in the pre-Transformer era, it has often been assumed that architectural and scale improvements would naturally solve it, and a systematic diagnostic across the modern vision stack remains absent. We provide such a diagnostic framework. We measure typicality bias via normalized pointwise mutual information (NPMI) over object pairs, and introduce STRANGE-Bench (Synthetic Typicality-RANked Grounded Evaluation Benchmark): a photorealistic, layout-controlled benchmark spanning 17 sub-tiers from typical to never-co-occurring object pairs. Across five model families (specialist detectors, open-vocabulary detectors, self-supervised, vision-language, and multimodal large language models) and three recognition tasks (supervised detection, open-vocabulary detection, and classification), the bias is prevalent: gaps of 5-11 p.p. persist when objects appear outside their typical company, and do not consistently shrink with scale. To mitigate it, we turn to data augmentation: existing augmentations are designed for visual diversity, not for breaking co-occurrence shortcuts, and sample from the very distribution that produces typicality bias. We propose Anchor-Atypicality Sampling (AAS), a simple sampling rule for paste-based augmentations that uses the NPMI signal to tilt the training-time co-occurrence distribution toward atypical partners. AAS reduces the typicality gap by up to 1.6 p.p. on natural-image COCO splits and 23.0 p.p. on synthetic STRANGE-Bench across three model families, without sacrificing overall performance.
items.title_ko: 낯선 것들: 전형적인 이웃 없이 나타나는 객체
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 시각 모델의 '전형성 편향(typicality bias)'을 다룹니다. 모델이 객체 자체의 시각적 특징보다는 전형적인 주변 환경에 의존하여 객체를 인식하는 경향이 있으며, 이러한 편향이 Transformer 시대에도 여전히 존재함을 체계적으로 진단합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 모델의 시각적 인식 오류의 원인 중 하나인 전형성 편향을 분석하여, 더 강건하고 정확한 객체 인식 모델을 개발하는 데 필요한 통찰을 제공합니다.

items.title: How Much Do Coding Agents Over-Edit, and Why? An Empirical Study of Unneeded Edits in Repository-Level Agent Patches
items.body: Agent patches are larger than developers', which is widely read as over-editing. But patch size does not say whether the extra edits are needed, what they are, or where they come from. We introduce Delta Residue Attribution (DRA), which replays agent trajectories, traces every block (unit) of the final patch to the step that wrote it, reverts each unit, and reruns the task tests to decide whether the unit is needed. We apply DRA to 7,660 resolved GitHub Copilot CLI trajectories from 18 frontier models on SWE-bench Verified (6,728) and DeepSWE (932), and grade developer patches using the same method. Agent patches do change more lines than developers'; on SWE-bench Verified the majority of extra edits add tests (61%) and documentation (13%) while on DeepSWE, most extra edits are code (58%). On both benchmarks, agents' code is on average at least as necessary as developers' (mean $NP_{code}$ 0.887 vs. 0.864 on SWE-bench Verified, where 11 of 18 models leave less unneeded code than developers, and 0.797 vs. 0.785 on DeepSWE). On average, 11% of an agent patch's code units on SWE-bench Verified are still unneeded, and 89% of those change behavior. Debug steps write almost none of the unneeded code. Code necessity differs substantially by model; it is unrelated to resolve rate on SWE-bench Verified and negatively correlated with it on DeepSWE (Spearman -0.59, p = 0.01). On SWE-bench Verified, pruning with DRA using only the tests the agent can see (its own tests and the repository's) removes the majority of unneeded code but also some needed code (67% recall, 46% precision), and 89% of pruned patches still resolve the task; asking the agent to audit its own diff is more precise but less effective (36% recall, 66% precision). We recommend that benchmarks report code necessity next to resolve rate and that over-editing be addressed through model training and harness-level pruning.
items.title_ko: 코딩 에이전트는 얼마나 과도하게 편집하는가, 그리고 그 이유는?
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 코딩 에이전트가 생성하는 패치에서 '과도한 편집(over-editing)' 문제를 경험적으로 분석합니다. Delta Residue Attribution (DRA)이라는 새로운 방법을 도입하여 에이전트의 패치 중 불필요한 편집이 무엇인지, 그리고 그 원인이 무엇인지 추적합니다. GitHub Copilot CLI의 7,660개 해결된 사례를 분석했습니다.
items.why_ko: AI 코딩 에이전트의 효율성과 신뢰성을 높이기 위해 불필요한 코드 변경을 줄이는 방법을 이해하는 데 중요하며, 에이전트의 행동을 분석하는 새로운 방법론을 제시합니다.

items.title: Shape-Aware Three-Way Merge for RDF Knowledge Graphs: The schema defines the conflict: an implementation and evaluation
items.body: Merging RDF serializations creates ordering conflicts and misses semantic ones. We describe and evaluate a three-way merge in which the schema defines a conflict: set algebra combines canonical triples, and a slot is contended only where a SHACL shape bounds its cardinality and both sides' changes cannot stand within that bound. Unbounded predicates union; contended slots go to a person. The same shapes graph validates the result. We do not claim the first three-way merge for RDF. Our contribution is an implementation in a production multi-agent store and an evaluation against a reimplementation of Quit Store's Context Merge overlap rule, which it extends rather than replaces, and six other strategies. Across five synthetic seeds, the shape-aware operator raised 33 conflicts, all true positives as judged by the same shapes that define them, with no triples lost or fabricated and no SHACL violations admitted. The context-overlap baseline, counted per slot, detected the same 33 conflicts but asked 845 questions. A replay built from recorded production incidents covers 105 human alias repairs (93 after excluding 12 chained pairs) and 939 duplicate-value incidents. It reproduces a triple-level limit: different names for one entity remain invisible (0 of 93 alias repairs detected, matching 0 of 21 synthetic cases). In a study of evolving shape contracts, merging shape declarations first handles the tested cardinality changes, while datatype evolution exposes a detector blind spot caught by post-merge validation. An oracle that reads no shapes agrees with the shipped operator on the facts and history of all 23 reachable single-slot cases. Under wrong shapes, a missing bound loses data silently and a spurious one only adds questions. The supported claim is fewer human decisions with nothing silently lost, for cardinality conflicts in one deployment, not general merge correctness.
items.title_ko: RDF 지식 그래프를 위한 Shape-Aware 세 방향 병합: 스키마가 충돌을 정의한다
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 RDF 직렬화의 병합 시 발생하는 순서 충돌 및 의미론적 충돌 문제를 해결하기 위한 'shape-aware' 세 방향 병합 방법을 제시합니다. SHACL 스키마를 사용하여 병합 충돌을 정의하고 해결하며, 정규화된 트리플 조합 및 제약 조건 내에서 변경 사항을 처리합니다.
items.why_ko: 복잡한 지식 그래프 데이터의 버전 관리와 협업을 위한 효과적인 병합 전략을 제시하여, 지식 그래프 기반 시스템 개발에 유용합니다.

items.title: A Survey of Security, Privacy, and Ethics of Large Language Models in Telecom
items.body: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into telecommunications for customer service, network analytics, and operational support. While offering efficiency and innovation, their deployment raises critical privacy, security, and ethical challenges due to the uniquely sensitive and longitudinal nature of telecom data. This paper presents a survey of LLM risks and safeguards in telecom context. Our survey introduces a telecom-specific taxonomy linking privacy, security, and ethics with use cases and outlines open research challenges such as longitudinal data privacy, cross-border compliance, and scalable guardrails.
items.title_ko: 통신 분야 대규모 언어 모델의 보안, 개인정보 보호 및 윤리 조사
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 통신 분야에서 LLM의 통합이 가져오는 중요한 개인정보 보호, 보안 및 윤리적 문제들을 조사합니다. 통신 데이터의 민감하고 장기적인 특성을 고려하여 LLM 위험 및 보호 조치에 대한 통신 산업 특화 분류 체계를 제시합니다.
items.why_ko: 민감한 개인 정보를 다루는 통신 산업에서 LLM의 안전하고 윤리적인 배포를 위한 가이드라인과 고려 사항을 제공하여, 관련 기술 개발에 중요한 시사점을 줍니다.

items.title: RePace: Reasoning about Demonstration Speedup for Faster Vision-Language-Action Policies
items.body: Since vision-language-action (VLA) policies can inherit the slow pace of human demonstrations, accelerating these demonstrations before fine-tuning can lead to faster VLA policies without an additional speed-selection module at deployment. Several offline speedup methods have focused on identifying segments that require less precision and assigning predefined speedup factors to the segments. However, even within a single segment, a speedup factor suitable for steady motion may be too high when precise alignment is required. To this end, this paper presents RePace, an offline reasoning framework that determines how much to accelerate each part of a demonstration. For the same recorded movement, RePace measures how much each candidate speedup factor shortens the sequence and compares the resulting observation-action pairs used for training. Given the task instruction, a pretrained language model uses the visual context and original motion of successive windows to interpret these candidate retiming effects and select a speedup profile for the complete episode. Experimental results demonstrate that RePace outperforms the baselines in overall task execution efficiency on both LIBERO and RoboCasa-Kitchen. On all three tasks with a gripper-equipped Franka Research 3 arm, RePace matches or exceeds the acceleration baselines in success rate and completes successful trials faster.
items.title_ko: RePace: 더 빠른 시각-언어-행동 정책을 위한 시연 속도 향상 추론
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 시각-언어-행동(VLA) 정책이 인간 시연의 느린 속도를 상속받는 문제를 해결하기 위해 RePace 방법을 제안합니다. 파인튜닝 전에 시연 속도를 가속화함으로써 추가적인 속도 선택 모듈 없이 더 빠른 VLA 정책을 만들 수 있음을 보여줍니다.
items.why_ko: 로봇이나 에이전트의 시각-언어-행동 정책이 인간처럼 자연스럽고 효율적으로 작동하도록 훈련하는 데 기여하며, 실제 환경에서의 적용 가능성을 높입니다.

items.title: Focus Only on What's Important: Training-Free Focus Maps for Frozen Vision Transformers in Long-Video Object Segmentation
items.body: Vision transformers are strong but costly image encoders for video object segmentation. Training-free token merging cuts compute uniformly across the frame, including on tracked objects. We give a frozen DINOv3 ViT inside a trained Cutie head a training-free focus map: full resolution where the segmenter expects its objects and coarser merging elsewhere. Protecting only the previous frame's mask works on short clips but fails on long videos, where fast motion pushes targets outside the margin and into background merging, locking in loss. Our policy instead takes the union of velocity-shifted and block-matched masks, runs a camera-compensated surprise check, delegates uncertain regions to the compared merger, and falls back to it when all objects are lost. On long videos (LVOS V2 valid, pre-specified protocol, three ViT-S seeds), it beats ALGM 0.98 by +2.76 J&F (95% object CI [+1.22,+4.44]; video-cluster [+0.99,+4.52]) at 16% fewer counted encoder FLOPs (0.385 vs. 0.459), sitting 1.0 J&F point below the dense-encoder baseline; at ViT-B the gain over ALGM 0.95 is +3.89 [+2.03,+5.87]. On DAVIS 2017 val it stays within -0.19 J&F of the dense encoder at ViT-S (-0.12 at ViT-B). Controls qualify the result: protecting only the previous mask under ALGM matches or exceeds accuracy at higher FLOPs (0.486), so expectation and surprise mainly reduce counted encoder compute. Practically, lower counted encoder compute did not reduce startup-inclusive mean Cutie step time on a 12-video LVOS sample (3%-8% lower in steady state; an equally engineered ALGM is faster at ViT-S and ViT-B). Section 5.2 separately examines a Cutie permanent-memory schedule and its latency and memory trade-offs. Code: https://github.com/boletoms/focused-cv
items.title_ko: 중요한 것에만 집중: 긴 영상 객체 분할을 위한 Frozen Vision Transformer용 Training-Free Focus Maps
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 비디오 객체 분할에서 Vision Transformer의 높은 계산 비용 문제를 해결하기 위해 '훈련 없는 포커스 맵(training-free focus map)'을 제시합니다. DINOv3 ViT에 이 포커스 맵을 적용하여, 분할기가 객체를 기대하는 영역은 고해상도로 유지하고 다른 영역은 거친 병합을 통해 컴퓨팅을 줄입니다.
items.why_ko: 긴 비디오에서 객체 분할 작업을 효율적으로 수행할 수 있는 방법을 제시하여, 비디오 처리 및 분석 분야의 실용적인 애플리케이션 개발에 기여합니다.

items.title: BOP-Refer: Benchmark for Monocular 3D and 2D Object Grounding
items.body: We introduce BOP-Refer, the first benchmark for monocular 3D and 2D grounding of everyday and industrial objects sourced from 9 diverse BOP datasets. We pair images from these datasets with VLM-generated and human-verified referring expressions, and derive accurate ground-truth 3D and 2D bounding boxes of the referred objects from their 3D models and 6DoF pose annotations. Our systematic evaluation of 17 frontier VLMs across the major proprietary and open-weight families (Gemini, GPT, Claude, Qwen, Gemma) shows that the best model, Gemini 4 Carbon, reaches 72.6% AP_IoU2D in 2D but only 12.4% AP_IoU3D in 3D, despite the more lenient IoU thresholds in 3D. The predicted 3D boxes are usually centered on the target objects in the image but often off in depth by more than the object's size, suggesting that metric scale estimation, which needs reliable object size priors, is currently by far the main source of error.
items.title_ko: BOP-Refer: 단안 3D 및 2D 객체 그라운딩 벤치마크
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 9개의 BOP 데이터셋에서 일상 및 산업용 객체의 단안 3D 및 2D 그라운딩을 위한 최초의 벤치마크인 BOP-Refer를 소개합니다. VLM(Vision-Language Model) 생성 및 인간 검증 참조 표현과 정확한 3D 및 2D 바운딩 박스를 제공하여, 최신 VLM의 성능을 체계적으로 평가합니다.
items.why_ko: 3D 및 2D 객체 그라운딩 작업의 표준화된 평가 기준을 제공하여, 멀티모달 AI 모델의 시각적 이해 및 참조 능력 개발에 중요한 기여를 합니다.

items.title: Model Weights, Airlocks and Sandboxes: A Call for Technical Validation of Re-identification Tests under the EDPB Anonymisation Guidelines
items.body: The Guidelines 02/2026 on anonymisation of the European Data Protection Board (EDPB), published for consultation in July 2026, assess anonymity relative to the entities that may access data. They bring AI models into scope and call for testing, but do not say how a re-identification test should be designed or validated, or how far its result counts as evidence. Building on our reply to the consultation, we describe a framework based on a secure processing environment whose outputs are reviewed before release (an airlock), and distinguish forms of release and three types of evidence: formal, empirical and indirect. We raise seven open questions, each with a scenario, and examine their technical side in three settings: the release of model weights (the trained parameters of a machine learning model), review at an airlock, and regulatory sandboxes, in which an authority supervises development and testing. In each setting the assessment depends on how far a test result can be relied on, since a failed re-identification attempt may mean only that the test was too weak. Drawing on measurement practice in other regulated fields, we call for re-identification tests to be validated as measurement methods, with stated detection limit, bias and uncertainty.
items.title_ko: 모델 가중치, 에어록, 샌드박스: EDPB 익명화 가이드라인 하의 재식별 테스트 기술 검증 요구
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 유럽 데이터 보호 이사회(EDPB)의 익명화 가이드라인에 따라 AI 모델의 익명성을 평가하고 재식별 테스트를 설계하고 검증하는 방법에 대한 프레임워크를 제시합니다. 안전한 처리 환경과 그 결과 검토를 기반으로 한 접근 방식을 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 모델이 개인 정보를 다룰 때 익명성 및 재식별 위험을 평가하고 관리하기 위한 기술적이고 실질적인 가이드라인을 제공하여, AI 시스템의 개인정보 보호 및 규제 준수에 필수적인 정보를 제공합니다.

items.title: From Prediction to Decision: Decision-Focused Fine-Tuning of Autoregressive Tabular Transformers for Cost-Sensitive Financial Events
items.body: Autoregressive transformers trained on tokenized tabular event streams are a simple and strong baseline for predicting financial events such as fraud. Yet institutions do not act on probabilities; they act on decisions whose consequences are asymmetric and heteroscedastic: the cost of a missed high-value fraud and that of a wrongly declined small purchase are not the same. The standard bridge is post-hoc Bayes-optimal thresholding of calibrated probabilities under a cost matrix. We ask whether fine-tuning the model to the decision objective can do better. We fine-tune the same pretrained model so that its restricted softmax over label tokens (already a distribution over business actions) maximizes expected utility under an institution-specified, amount-scaled cost matrix. Because the reward is a known function of (action, outcome, amount) and the outcome is observed in the data, the expected-utility objective and its gradient are available in closed form. This is example-dependent cost-sensitive learning whose per-example loss is linear in the predicted probability, with no sampling, critics, or advantage estimation. A KL anchor to the pretrained model and an auxiliary language-modeling term preserve calibration and the generative event model. A sampled, group-normalized (GRPO-style) variant provides the extension point to trajectory-level rewards.
items.title_ko: 예측에서 결정으로: 비용 민감 금융 이벤트를 위한 자기회귀형 테이블 트랜스포머의 결정 중심 파인튜닝
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 금융 이벤트 예측을 위한 자기회귀형 테이블 트랜스포머의 '결정 중심 파인튜닝'을 제안합니다. 예측 확률에 사후적으로 비용 행렬을 적용하는 대신, 모델 훈련 단계에서부터 비대칭적인 의사결정 비용을 직접 고려하여 파인튜닝하는 방법을 탐구합니다.
items.why_ko: 금융 분야에서 AI 모델의 예측 정확도를 넘어, 실제 비즈니스 결정의 비용-효과성을 최적화하는 방법을 제시하여, 실용적인 AI 의사결정 시스템 개발에 중요한 통찰을 제공합니다.

items.title: DRBench Pro: A Knowledge-Centric Benchmark for Professional Deep Research Agents
items.body: Deep research agents gather information from multiple sources and synthesize it into reports on complex, open-ended questions. Existing benchmarks assess report quality along several dimensions, but lack a dedicated knowledge-centric evaluation of which research directions a report covers and how deeply it explores them. We introduce DRBench Pro, a benchmark that makes structured knowledge coverage the primary evaluation target. Our automated pipeline builds local knowledge trees from Wikipedia and uses sampled subgraphs to generate research queries and evidence-grounded rubrics. Each rubric corresponds to a relation in the tree, preserving the structure of the knowledge being evaluated. Agents receive only the research query. This structure allows us to measure breadth across major research directions and depth along related knowledge chains, with their geometric mean giving overall coverage. The benchmark includes 144 cases across 24 domains and 44,102 rubrics. Evaluating 16 deep research agents reveals different strengths in breadth and depth, with the best-performing agent reaching 57.04% overall coverage. Rubric judgments agree closely with human annotations, and agent rankings remain stable across the tested metric configurations.
items.title_ko: DRBench Pro: 전문가 심층 연구 에이전트를 위한 지식 중심 벤치마크
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 복잡하고 개방형 질문에 대한 심층 연구 에이전트의 지식 커버리지와 탐색 깊이를 평가하는 새로운 벤치마크인 DRBench Pro를 소개합니다. Wikipedia에서 지식 트리를 구축하고 이를 통해 보고서의 구조화된 지식 커버리지를 주된 평가 목표로 삼습니다.
items.why_ko: AI 연구 에이전트의 '심층적인 이해와 탐구' 능력을 평가하는 새로운 기준을 제시하여, 실제 과학 연구 및 복잡한 정보 탐색 분야에서의 AI 에이전트 발전에 중요한 기여를 합니다.

items.title: Put the World Back: Timestamps Matter in Time Series Reasoning
items.body: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to time series reasoning. However, current evaluations often give models events in chronological order and already matched to the time series. This makes it unclear whether models use timestamps to connect events with observations or simply take shortcuts. To expose this ambiguity, we reformulate time series reasoning from a world-to-series projection perspective, viewing timestamps as explicit indices that connect numerical observations and external events to shared world states. We identify three structures that timestamps can make explicit: temporal causal structure, time semantics, and event-series alignment. Building on this perspective, we develop a diagnostic protocol that distinguishes timestamp-grounded reasoning from correlational shortcuts, a distinction that accuracy-based benchmarks cannot make. Controlled interventions on 310 questions from two tasks show that high accuracy can persist when timestamps are replaced by relative offsets or removed, while breaking event-series alignment induces systematic failures. When context is pre-aligned, models barely need timestamps. When order is missing, they use dates to recall world knowledge. Without dates, they rely on correlational shortcuts and rarely notice incorrect timestamps. These findings show that high accuracy on pre-aligned, ordered inputs does not establish that a model uses timestamps to synchronize observations with the world. We release our code, model outputs, and trajectory labels at https://github.com/tingrui-huang/timestamps-matter.
items.title_ko: 세상을 다시 제자리로: 시계열 추론에서 타임스탬프의 중요성
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 대규모 언어 모델(LLM)이 시계열 추론에서 타임스탬프를 어떻게 활용하는지 탐구합니다. 현재 평가 방식이 모델이 타임스탬프를 사용하는지, 아니면 단순히 지름길을 택하는지 불분명하게 만든다는 점을 지적하며, 타임스탬프를 수치 관측값과 이벤트를 연결하는 명시적 인덱스로 간주하는 새로운 관점을 제시합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 시계열 데이터 처리 능력을 보다 정확하게 평가하고 개선하기 위한 새로운 프레임워크를 제공하여, 시계열 데이터 분석 및 예측 분야의 AI 적용에 중요한 통찰을 줍니다.

items.title: Probing Visual Idiosyncrasies in Text-to-Image Models
items.body: Text-to-Image (T2I) models turn short text descriptions into images, and the leading models now produce images of comparable visual quality. Whether their outputs still carry model-specific characteristics matters for attribution, for model comparison beyond aggregate quality, and for evaluations that assume anonymity. We ask whether images from frontier T2I models can still be classified by source, and which visual properties make this possible. Here we show that a standard ResNet-50 identifies the source of an image among HiDream-O1-Dev, FLUX.2-dev, HunyuanImage-3.0, and Qwen-Image-2512, the four highest-ranked open-source models on the Text-to-Image Arena, with 100.00% accuracy on held-out prompts. Human participants reach only 62.61% on the pairwise version of this task, so the distinguishing cues are not visually obvious. They are also not tied to a particular classifier and survive severe image corruptions and out-of-distribution prompts. We trace them to visual idiosyncrasies at three levels. Low-level texture statistics alone let a lightweight multi-layer perceptron match ResNet-50. Object layout, depth, and albedo estimated from the images each carry a source signal. Image captions reveal model-specific preferences in style and background that the prompts never specify. A one-sentence hint about these cues raises human accuracy by 9.03 percentage points. These idiosyncrasies make source classification a tool for measuring similarity between models and between real and generated images, and they caution against assuming anonymity in human preference evaluation of T2I models.
items.title_ko: 텍스트-이미지 모델의 시각적 특이성 탐지
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 최신 텍스트-이미지(T2I) 모델이 생성하는 이미지가 여전히 모델 특유의 시각적 특성을 가지고 있는지를 조사합니다. 표준 ResNet-50 모델이 선도적인 T2I 모델의 이미지를 소스별로 분류할 수 있음을 보여주며, 이러한 분류를 가능하게 하는 시각적 속성을 분석합니다.
items.why_ko: 생성된 이미지의 출처를 파악하고 모델 간 비교 및 평가를 고도화하는 데 필요한 시각적 특성을 이해하는 데 도움을 줍니다.

items.title: Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent: Self-Structuring Learning through Question Answering
items.body: We consider the problem of constructing knowledge bases for applications based on large language models, in which the structure of a knowledge base determines how an application can retrieve and connect the information needed to answer a question. We study Self-Structuring Learning, a setting in which questions and expected answers guide the construction of a persistent knowledge base whose editable structure can be a graph schema or the organization of linked knowledge documents. We propose Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent, which diagnoses discrepancies between expected answers and responses obtained through the current knowledge base. At each round, the method proposes a structural edit, rebuilds the knowledge base, and adopts the edit when the learning loss decreases. The retained structure is evaluated on other questions about the same sources. By randomizing over candidate edits, we express the loss change of an edit as a derivative with respect to the probability of selecting it, and we evaluate joint edits as single candidates because their changes interact. Schema Descent instantiates the method for graph schemas. In experiments on large documents, each a bundle of research papers, the updated knowledge cards and graph schemas obtain higher mean Answer F1 on held-out generated questions than their initial structures, with schema gains in every document. On human questions, mean F1 rises for schemas and falls for cards: the updated structures serve the kind of question they were learned from.

items.title: Provably Efficient Offline Discounted Reinforcement Learning under Recursive Entropic Risk
items.body: We study risk-sensitive reinforcement learning in finite discounted infinite-horizon Markov Decision Processes with recursive entropic risk measures (ERM), parameterized by $β\neq 0$. We consider both risk-averse ($β>0$) and risk-seeking ($β<0$) settings. We consider the offline RL setting, where the agent is provided with a fixed dataset and wishes to learn a near-optimal policy using this dataset. We introduce a model-based algorithm, called ERM Value Iteration Lower Confidence Bound (ERM-VI-LCB) and derive a PAC-type bound on its sample complexity. We also establish a corresponding lower bound, demonstrating that exponential dependence on $|β|/(1-γ)$ asserted by the upper bound is unavoidable in the worst case. The presented bounds provide the first rigorous sample complexity guarantees for offline RL under recursive ERM across both risk-averse and risk-seeking regimes.
items.title_ko: 재귀 엔트로피 위험 하의 오프라인 할인 강화 학습에 대한 증명 가능한 효율성
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 재귀 엔트로피 위험 측정(ERM)을 사용하는 유한 할인 무한 수평 마르코프 의사결정 과정(MDP)에서 위험 민감 강화 학습을 연구합니다. 오프라인 RL 설정에서 주어진 데이터셋을 사용하여 준최적 정책을 학습하는 모델 기반 알고리즘인 ERM 값 반복 하한 경계(ERM-VI-LCB)를 소개합니다.
items.why_ko: 오프라인 강화 학습에서 위험 민감성을 고려한 효율적인 알고리즘을 제시하여, 금융, 의료 등 위험 관리가 중요한 분야의 RL 적용에 기여합니다.

items.title: Proverbs As A Window On Collective Prescriptions
items.body: Proverbs, as repositories of traditional wisdom, have informed human reasoning for millennia. Yet the collective prescriptions they encode have remained largely unquantified. We introduce a computational framework to analyze nearly 50,000 English-language proverbs. Using large language models, validated against human judgments, we map the topical landscape of proverbs, assess their prescriptive power, and quantify their recommendations on key dimensions of human judgment and behavior. We find that most proverbs are prescriptive, offering guidance in domains under individual control, such as preparation and prudent action, whereas proverbs about uncontrollable circumstances, such as fate and mortality, tend to describe rather than prescribe. When prescriptive proverbs take a consistent stance, they favor caution over risk, long-term over short-term outcomes, honesty over deception, and kindness over malice, and show a moderate tendency toward suspicion over trust. On dimensions involving genuine trade-offs, especially autonomy versus compliance, proverbs provide contradicting advice rather than a single recommendation. This analysis provides a quantitative map of the collective prescriptions in a culture's proverbial wisdom, revealing a core of prudent, honest, and forward-looking guidance alongside varied advice where circumstances dictate the best course of action.
items.title_ko: 속담을 통해 본 집단적 규범
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 약 50,000개의 영어 속담을 분석하여 집단적 규범을 정량화하는 계산 프레임워크를 소개합니다. 대규모 언어 모델을 사용하여 속담의 주제, 규범적 힘, 그리고 인간의 판단 및 행동에 대한 권장 사항을 매핑하고 정량화합니다.
items.why_ko: AI를 활용하여 인간 사회의 문화적, 윤리적 규범을 이해하고 분석하는 새로운 접근 방식을 제시하여, 사회과학과 AI의 융합 연구에 기여합니다.

items.title: Repairing the Trustworthiness of Distilled Language Models
items.body: Knowledge distillation enables the deployment of large language models through smaller student models, but the compression process can introduce regressions in trustworthiness even when downstream performance is preserved. Repairing such failures is challenging because the original distillation corpus is often unavailable, while direct preference optimization may alter capabilities inherited from the teacher. We propose a targeted repair framework based on the proximal Bregman response function (PBRF) that addresses both limitations. We estimate the curvature required for PBRF using a surrogate proxy dataset, removing dependence on the original transfer corpus, and extend the framework to preference-based supervision through an odds-ratio objective. This enables the use of preferred and dispreferred response pairs while constraining changes to the distilled model. Our results show that the proposed approach improves targeted trustworthiness behaviors for both pre-training and post-training models while largely preserving downstream performance, providing a practical alternative to re-distillation or unconstrained preference optimization. Our experiment results show that across different distilled models, the trustworthy regression can be improved by up to 8% with less than 1% decrement in perplexity.
items.title_ko: 증류된 언어 모델의 신뢰성 복구
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 지식 증류(knowledge distillation)를 통해 소형화된 언어 모델에서 발생하는 신뢰성 저하 문제를 해결하기 위한 '표적 복구 프레임워크'를 제안합니다. 원래 증류 코퍼스가 없는 상황에서, 프록시 Bregman 반응 함수를 기반으로 하여 파라미터 지식을 유지하면서 신뢰성 실패를 복구합니다.
items.why_ko: 소형화된 LLM의 성능은 유지하면서도 신뢰성 문제를 해결하는 실용적인 방법을 제시하여, 경량화된 AI 모델의 안전하고 윤리적인 배포에 기여합니다.

items.title: Not all world models can doubt: how training objective and architecture shape epistemic uncertainty in JEPA and RSSM world models
items.body: World models predict how an environment responds to actions, so that candidate actions can be evaluated before execution. Executed actions, or decisions, taken in this manner are only as reliable as the model's predictive capabilities, and predictions in turn are only reliable within the model's experience. Epistemic uncertainty (EU) is the signal that marks where that experience ends. In this work we offer an extensive empirical study on how training objectives and architectures shape epistemic uncertainty of world models. More precisely, we present a controlled comparison of post-hoc EU (last-layer Laplace and ensembles) between two dominant models of different paradigms: 1) LeWorldModel (LeWM): A joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA), which predicts the next embedding without a decoder, and 2) DreamerV3: A recurrent state-space model (RSSM), which reconstructs the observation from a recurrent latent state. In ten simulated visual-control environments, we follow a controlled state perturbation of the environment state through every stage of the models up to the final EU estimate. We find that the RSSM attenuates the state perturbation through two mechanisms before it reaches an estimator on the predictor feature. Its recurrent update averages over context, so a change in a single frame reaches the state at a fraction of its size and recovers only as the change persists. Its reconstruction objective weights an entity by the pixels it covers, so a small object can be lost due to the training objective. The JEPA has neither mechanism and passes the change through all stages to the uncertainty. We further show that this translates to gaps in five uncertainty related downstream tasks, from unfamiliar-state detection to uncertainty-penalised planning: the RSSM uncertainty misses deviations that its own posterior registers, whereas the JEPA uncertainty reports what its model sees.
items.title_ko: 모든 월드 모델이 의심할 수 있는 것은 아니다: JEPA 및 RSSM 월드 모델에서 훈련 목표와 아키텍처가 인식적 불확실성을 형성하는 방식
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 월드 모델(world model)의 '인식적 불확실성(epistemic uncertainty)'이 훈련 목표와 아키텍처에 의해 어떻게 형성되는지 광범위하게 탐구합니다. JEPA(Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture)와 RSSM(Recurrent State Space Model) 월드 모델을 대상으로 훈련 목표가 모델의 경험 한계를 표시하는 신호인 인식적 불확실성에 어떤 영향을 미치는지 분석합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 에이전트가 자신의 지식 한계를 인식하고 '모른다'고 말할 수 있는 능력을 이해하는 것은 안전하고 신뢰할 수 있는 AI 시스템을 구축하는 데 필수적입니다.

items.title: Gradient TD($λ$) for Non-Linear Function Approximation
items.body: Temporal difference (TD) learning is central to reinforcement learning. Many methods use semi-gradient TD, which may diverge, or develop algorithms with mean-squared Bellman or TD-error objectives that are difficult to analyze. Gradient TD algorithms overcome these challenges by using projection of the value function and present convergent off-policy algorithms. However, the algorithm for $λ$-return was limited to linear function approximation. Here, we extend the same to non-linear function approximation, which is desirable since many strong modern function approximators are complex and non-linear. Recent works have derived similar algorithms with a generalized projected Bellman error objective. Alternatively, we continue working with the projected Bellman error.
items.title_ko: 비선형 함수 근사를 위한 Gradient TD($\lambda$)
items.why_ko: 강화 학습에서 더 복잡한 비선형 모델을 사용하여 가치 함수를 근사할 수 있는 이론적 기반을 제공하여, 다양한 RL 애플리케이션의 성능 향상에 기여합니다.

items.title: Routeability Before Routing: Routeability Audit Protocol (RAP) and RouteabilityBench for Audited LLM Model Selection
items.body: LLM routing aims to choose, for each prompt, which model in a portfolio is most likely to answer correctly. This only makes sense when the benchmark contains enough prompt-specific variation for different models to be best on different inputs. On coarse-scored LLM benchmarks, however, many models often tie for the best score, and the single best model may already leave little room for improvement. We therefore propose a routeability-first audit, instantiated as RAP and RouteabilityBench, a runnable claim-verification package. The audit is retrospective: it runs once the benchmark-portfolio score matrix exists and before router comparisons are interpreted as general evidence, rather than certifying a portfolio that has not yet been evaluated. Across four benchmarks and 66 LLMs, generic routing enhancements such as larger embedding sets, dimensionality reduction, selective abstention, clustering, and stronger regressors do not consistently outperform the single best model. The clearest positive evidence is concentrated in portfolio-dependent Omni-MATH settings, while GPQA, MMLU-Pro, and IFEval show different ways in which routing can remain hard or predictor-sensitive. Our practical recommendation is that routing gains should be reported together with routeability diagnostics, tied-best analysis, portfolio construction details, and family-corrected statistical tests.
items.title_ko: 라우팅 전에 라우팅 가능성: 감사를 통한 LLM 모델 선택을 위한 RAP 및 RouteabilityBench
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 LLM 라우팅의 전제 조건인 '라우팅 가능성(routeability)'에 대한 감사를 제안합니다. RAP(Routeability Audit Protocol)과 RouteabilityBench를 통해 벤치마크에 프롬프트별 충분한 변동성이 있는지, 그리고 여러 모델이 최적 점수에서 동점을 이루지 않는지를 평가하여, 의미 있는 LLM 라우팅이 가능하도록 돕습니다.
items.why_ko: 여러 LLM 중 최적의 모델을 선택하는 라우팅 시스템의 효율성과 유효성을 높이기 위한 중요한 전처리 단계를 제시하여, 실제 LLM 서비스의 성능 향상에 기여합니다.

items.title: The Linguistic Knowledge Benchmark: Do Language Models Know the Foundations of Early-Grade Literacy?
items.body: Many languages of instruction in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) are poorly represented in the data used to train language models. Before these models can support early-grade literacy in such languages, we need to know whether they hold the linguistic knowledge of each language that literacy teaching relies on. To test this, we present the Linguistic Knowledge Benchmark and the reproducible, largely automated pipeline that turns curriculum documents, teacher guides and pupil books into a vetted question set organised on a fixed grid of nine linguistic domains and seven grade levels. The pipeline combines LLM-driven source survey, feature consolidation, item generation and quality control with an item-selection step inspired by item response theory and a final expert review. We instantiate it for Kiswahili (Kenya; 135 items) and English (United Kingdom; 137 items) and evaluate 121 and 119 models respectively. Frontier models exceed 90% accuracy in both languages, but accuracy falls steeply for smaller and cheaper models, and more so in Kiswahili. The two best models under 10 billion parameters reach 91.7% and 73.0% in English but only 51.9% and 40.7% in Kiswahili, and the mean accuracy of models deployable on mobile and tablet hardware is 47% in English against 24% in Kiswahili. The models most practical for low-resource classrooms are therefore the least capable in the languages they would serve. We release a 20-item sample per language, all pipeline prompts, open-source code, and a public leaderboard. This is the first rung of a three-level evaluation ladder for measuring and generating decodable text to support foundational literacy.
items.title_ko: 언어 지식 벤치마크: 언어 모델은 초등 문해력의 기초를 아는가?
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 저소득 및 중간 소득 국가(LMIC)에서 사용되는 언어들의 문해력 교육을 지원하기 위해, 언어 모델이 해당 언어의 언어학적 지식을 얼마나 가지고 있는지 평가하는 '언어 지식 벤치마크(Linguistic Knowledge Benchmark)'를 제시합니다. 교육 과정 문서, 교사 가이드 등을 활용하여 자동화된 파이프라인으로 벤치마크를 구축합니다.
items.why_ko: 다양한 언어, 특히 자원 부족 언어에 대한 LLM의 교육적 활용 가능성을 평가하고 개선하기 위한 중요한 도구를 제공하여, 교육 기술의 포괄적인 발전에 기여합니다.

items.title: LoopTitan: What Does Parameter Revisit Buy a Mixture-of-Experts?
items.body: Looped Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures revisit layer parameters across depths. This design increases effective depth without adding parameters. Recent looped MoE studies report substantial gains over the standard MoE at matched budgets (parameters, FLOPs and KV cache). However, the reported gains still confound parameter revisit with other design choices, e.g., network shape and residual scale. We ask, what does parameter revisit itself buy? Using matched non-revisit controls, we find that parameter revisit itself buys almost nothing. We argue that revisit only offers a freedom an MoE already has, i.e., trading experts for depth (more layers, fewer experts each) at fixed parameters. First, at matched budgets, we decompose the state-of-the-art looped recipe, with revisit last. A non-revisit control retains all the gain. Most comes from network shape, and the rest from residual scale. We prove this scale acts as a lower learning rate on revisited layers. This helps under AdamW's uneven layer step sizes, but disappears under Muon, which keeps them nearly equal. Second, beyond matched budgets, we evaluate revisit by adding compute at fixed parameters. One extra visit gains more than doubling the experts. Yet without revisit, a deeper standard MoE at equal parameters and compute obtains 90.2% of that gain under Muon.
